basis_reporting.basis: all-fragments (n_L=44 for Go; common-basis figure requires the other nine languages' fragment sets, not available to this shard)

complexity_counting_rule_frozen_before_a.context_dependent_rules: Count each documented Go semantic rule whose outcome depends on context beyond the local syntax (e.g. platform int width, slice capacity/aliasing after append, map iteration order, nil-interface-vs-nil-concrete-value comparison).
complexity_counting_rule_frozen_before_a.distinct_syntax_forms: Count each distinct Go surface syntax construct (keyword, operator, or stdlib call form) that a reader must recognize to correctly interpret at least one supported probe's fragment, counted once regardless of how many probes reuse it.
complexity_counting_rule_frozen_before_a.documented_semantic_exceptions: Count each named exception to an otherwise general rule that Go's own specification/documentation states explicitly (e.g. integer division-by-zero panics but float division-by-zero yields Inf/NaN; signed integer overflow wraps by spec rather than being undefined; comparing uncomparable interface values panics at runtime; Go 1.22 changed for-loop variable scoping).
complexity_counting_rule_frozen_before_a.implicit_rules: Count each documented Go behavior that occurs without a dedicated token at the use site (e.g. zero-value initialization, structural interface satisfaction, automatic slice header copy-by-value while sharing backing array, GC-driven deallocation, loop-variable-per-iteration semantics).

context_dependent_rules: platform-dependent int width
slice aliasing vs copy after append reallocation
map iteration order unspecified
nil interface vs typed-nil-inside-interface comparison
integer division panics, float division does not
channel direction restricts send/receive
pointer vs value receiver changes method set and mutation visibility
escape analysis decides stack vs heap allocation (invisible at call site)
goroutine scheduling order is unspecified
struct comparability depends on field types
array vs slice value semantics differ (copy vs shared) though syntactically similar
string to []byte conversion copies, but iteration over string yields runes not bytes
unexported struct fields are invisible and unsettable from another package
interface satisfaction is structural, so which methods count depends on the full method set at the point of assignment
generic type inference outcome depends on all call-site argument types together
defer argument evaluation is immediate but call is deferred
race-freedom of an operation depends on whether sync/atomic or mutex actually wraps every access site, not on syntax alone
cgo build behavior depends on CGO_ENABLED environment variable
map read on nil map returns zero value, write on nil map panics
append may or may not mutate the underlying array depending on capacity
closures over loop variables changed semantics between pre- and post-1.22 toolchains
documented_semantic_exceptions: int/int division panics on divide-by-zero, float/float division yields +Inf/-Inf/NaN
signed integer overflow wraps per spec (defined), unlike C's UB
comparing two interface values with uncomparable dynamic types panics at runtime even though '==' compiles
a nil map is safe to read (zero value) but panics on write, exception to the general 'operations on nil are safe' expectation
array types are comparable with '==' if element type is comparable, but slices/maps/functions are never comparable
a method with a pointer receiver is not in the method set of a value, an exception to the general 'method set determined by declared receiver type' when substituting into an interface
Go 1.22 changed for-loop variable semantics (new variable per iteration) as a documented breaking exception from earlier versions
deferred function argument evaluation happens immediately at the defer statement rather than at call time, an exception to normal call-time evaluation
const numeric expressions are untyped and can overflow-check at compile time even though runtime int arithmetic wraps silently, a documented split behavior
struct field visibility crosses package boundaries via reflection/encoding even though normal code access is blocked, a documented exception used by encoding/json etc.
recover() only has an effect when called directly inside a deferred function, an exception to ordinary function-call semantics
an empty struct{} occupies zero bytes in most cases, an exception to typical struct sizing rules
unbuffered channel send/receive synchronizes (happens-before) by spec, whereas buffered channels only synchronize up to capacity, a documented exception
cgo call overhead and goroutine stack switching is a documented deviation from normal Go call performance/semantics
comparing NaN floats is always false including NaN==NaN, following IEEE754 rather than Go's usual reflexive equality expectation
implicit_rules: zero-value initialization for every declared-but-unassigned variable
implicit dereference is NOT performed by Go (explicit *p required) but implicit method-set promotion IS (embedded struct fields/methods promoted without a syntax marker)
garbage collection reclaims heap objects with no destructor call visible in source
slice header (ptr,len,cap) copy-by-value at call sites while backing array is shared
structural interface satisfaction requires no 'implements' declaration
defer statements execute in LIFO order at function return, not at the defer statement site
goroutine leaks are possible with no compiler diagnostic
return of named result variables can be implicit (bare 'return')
map growth/rehashing invalidates no iterator state contract implicitly
conversion between compatible named types can be implicit within generic type inference
panic unwinds the stack silently through intervening frames unless recovered
append reallocation choice (grow vs reuse) is implicit
unexported fields are zero-valued when decoded across package/reflection boundaries silently
method value/method expression binding captures receiver implicitly
string immutability is enforced by the type system without a mutability keyword
comparable constraint checking for generic type parameters happens implicitly at instantiation
integer to floating point conversions can silently lose precision for large values
embedding promotes fields/methods without redeclaration
channel close semantics allow receive-after-close to yield zero value silently
the blank identifier '_' silently discards values
multiple return values require explicit multi-assignment, but error must be explicitly checked or is silently ignorable
struct literal field zero-fill for omitted fields
array bounds are part of the type and checked implicitly, unlike slices
interface method dispatch is a hidden vtable-style indirection with no explicit dispatch syntax
generic instantiation may cause implicit specialization vs boxing depending on compiler version
sync.WaitGroup's Add/Done/Wait ordering contract is documented but not enforced by syntax

The reported requirement score (46) is a provisional monotonic placeholder computed as round(100/(1+raw)) = round(100/2.1707) = 46, preserving 'lower raw value => higher normalized score'. The runner must recompute the final 0-100 figure once all ten languages' raw capability_efficiency values are merged, per spec 6.1.4.E and the common-basis/all-fragments reporting requirement.
